extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, legislators, reformers, and informed public interested in national economic and labor policy
extracted.subtask_short: policy on taxation and labor organization
extracted.subtask_description: Normative policy guidance for national taxation (inheritance, corporate) and for the organization, recognition, and regulation of labor unions, including suggested legal and administrative arrangements. Targets national/state/municipal government action and labor/employer practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduated inheritance tax
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a graduated inheritance tax to mitigate existing inequalities in wealth; preserve public interest without doing injustice to owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification: existing fortunes should not be preserved intact beyond certain amounts; such a tax can mitigate inequalities and guarantee public service for more of the wealth. Practical considerations: severity should be dictated chiefly by conditions of practical efficiency; the tax should be imposed exclusively by the Federal government to prevent evasion; the tax at its highest level could be placed without danger of evasion at as much as twenty per cent; examples given: the United Kingdom raises almost $100,000,000 from such a source and a slightly increased scale might double that amount for the American Treasury. Special measures: property placed in trust for heirs above a certain amount should face an exceptionally severe deduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal (central) imposition of inheritance tax
rubrics_metrics.description: Inheritance tax should be imposed exclusively by the Federal government rather than by states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: state inheritance taxes sufficiently large to accomplish desired results will be evaded by changes of residence; a Federal tax at a high level is less vulnerable to evasion, and foreign residence evasion is limited by severe foreign inheritance laws. While taxes should be uniform and laid by the central government, the proceeds need not be appropriated exclusively by the Federal Treasury — a proportionate share of net receipts could be distributed to states based on yield from their residents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduated income tax is inferior for this object
rubrics_metrics.description: A graduated income tax is less efficient and less equitable for addressing inherited wealth and socialized value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasoning: it taxes the man who earns the money as well as the inheritor; it taxes earned income as well as income from investments and cannot discriminate effectively as to the source of investment income. Moreover, it would interfere with a more serviceable plan of taxing corporate net profits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax net profits of corporations under federal jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Tax the net profits of corporations subject to the jurisdiction of the Federal government as part of constructive corporate regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This plan is described as indispensable for constructive treatment of corporate problems; corporate and inheritance taxes should be uniform throughout the country and laid by the central government to enable effective control over corporations and the 'money power.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity of corporation and inheritance taxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporation and inheritance taxes should be uniform throughout the country and laid by the central government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While uniform and centrally laid, there is no absolute necessity that the Federal government exclusively appropriate all proceeds; a fixed proportion of net receipts could be distributed to the states, estimated per state on the net yield derived from its residents.

rubrics_metrics.name: State appropriation of value created by community
rubrics_metrics.description: The government should separate and appropriate that fraction of the total economic product which is created by social rather than individual activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: semi-monopolistic organization of industries enables the state to claim a part of value made by the community; democracy should secure those social-created elements of value for public benefit. This underlies justification for inheritance/corporate taxation and other public appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severe deduction on trusts that demoralize heirs
rubrics_metrics.description: Property placed in trust for heirs above a certain amount (especially trusts that perpetuate irresponsibility) should be subject to an exceptionally severe deduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: trusts often produce parasitic heirs who lack economic responsibility; while forbidding such testamentary arrangements outright may be too radical for public opinion, taxation can be used to penalize devices that intentionally demoralize future generations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal recognition and favorable discrimination for labor unions
rubrics_metrics.description: Labor unions should receive legal recognition and substantial discrimination in their favor by the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: unions are the most effective machinery yet created for improving the economic and social condition of laborers, raising standards of living, and mitigating destructive competition. Recognition should be framed as a preference for organization over disorganized individual labor. However, recognition is not unconditional: it should be given to unions that contribute to the general economic interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional recognition: unions must promote efficiency and individual opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: State recognition of labor unions must depend upon their conformity to conditions imposed in the interest of efficiency and individual economic independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit quote guidance: 'Your recognition... must depend upon conformity to another set of conditions, imposed in the interest of efficiency and individual economic independence.' The state will recognize unions that contribute to the general economic interest and will refuse/oppose unions whose rules and methods are inimical to that interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active suppression of 'bad' unions
rubrics_metrics.description: Refuse legal recognition and aggressively oppose unions whose rules and methods are inimical to the public economic interest; deny employment to their members and organize counter-unions where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures proposed: aggressive and relentless legal/political opposition; employment denial for members of such unions; organization of counter-unions in trades where bad unions are dominant. Purpose is to fit labor organization into a national economic system and to prevent unions from becoming industrial factions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unions' right to demand minimum wage and minimum working day via collective bargaining
rubrics_metrics.description: Unions should be permitted to demand and secure by collective bargaining a minimum wage and a minimum working day (varying by trade, branch, region, and season).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These agreements should be absolute within the limits contained in the bond. The unions are expected to make the best terms possible through collective bargaining; such minima protect labor standards while leaving scope for individual advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum pay and overtime left to individual arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Collective bargaining should set minima, but maximum pay/work and overtime arrangements should be left to individual employer-employee agreements, with overtime paid at one-and-one-half to two times ordinary rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: employers should be able to reward exceptional workers above the minimum, and workers should be allowed to work overtime if properly compensated. In return for privileged positions the unions should abandon restrictive rules that prevent such individual arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employers' right to resist artificial restriction of labor supply
rubrics_metrics.description: If an employer employs only union men, he should have the right to demand that the supply of labor not be artificially restricted and to rely on procuring as much labor as business growth requires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects employers from union-imposed artificial scarcity of labor and supports efficient business operation. Collective agreements should provide terms upon admission to unions and ensure adequate labor supply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection between unions and trade schools; state support for apprenticeship training
rubrics_metrics.description: In all skilled trades, unions should have close connections to trade schools, and the state should ensure instruction is of the highest quality and furnish it free to as many apprentices as trade agreements permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: improving labor efficiency and training is a public interest. State involvement in trade education supports both union standards and national economic efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference by state and municipal governments for union labor and discrimination among unions
rubrics_metrics.description: State and municipal governments should, insofar as they have power, give preference to union labor while discriminating between 'good' and 'bad' unions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges constitutional/legal constraints but argues municipal/state preference would encourage employers toward a constructive labor policy. Although politically difficult, such discrimination would support employers and unions that stand for efficiency and individual opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal mechanisms to reduce strikes and require conciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt laws (modeled on recent Canadian legislation) to ensure no strike takes place until every effort has been made to reach a fair understanding or compromise and to allow public opinion to judge the merits of controversies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: making the consequences of warfare (strikes/lock-outs) increasingly dangerous will deter frivolous conflict; requiring conciliation, publicity, and procedures to assess controversies will reduce strike frequency. The state could also use discreet supervision to make strikes less likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer unionization even at expense of excluding non-union laborers
rubrics_metrics.description: Public policy should decisively prefer labor organization over impartiality between union and non-union labor; non-union industrial laborers may be excluded from trades to preserve standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: impartiality is impracticable and expediently harmful; non-union laborers often act as industrial derelicts who undercut standards. Where necessary, exclusion of non-union labor is justified to prevent degradation of standards of living and to promote collective independence through association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate labor supply to benefit agriculture and distribute labor efficiently
rubrics_metrics.description: Organized labor should lead to a regulated, less fluid labor supply that stabilizes agricultural labor and channels less-trained workers to healthier farm employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: current instability sees agricultural workers flood cities in prosperous times and depress wages in downturns. By regulating supply and enhancing efficiency, agriculture can retain necessary labor, reduce costs of living, and provide better prospects for less-trained workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor organization as transitional device toward better labor-training and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed labor reorganization is at best a transitional method toward a more perfect future system of labor training, distribution, and compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveat: the plan is not an ultimate solution but supplements tendencies toward formation of improved labor and institutional reforms. Fully embodied legal institutions would likely require constitutional changes and broader political regeneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: State appropriation of fruits of monopoly where capital combines
rubrics_metrics.description: Where combination of capital (monopoly) is economically necessary, the state is bound to appropriate the fruits of its monopoly for public purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: combination of capital increases social contribution to value; the state should secure that portion of the economic product created by social activity for public benefit, complementing labor organization and inheritance/corporate taxation policies.
